text: GPU on-demand pricing is already steep, which makes the spot discount tempting the moment you see it. But spot GPUs come with a real tradeoff for training specifically, and understanding it precisely is what separates a smart cost decision from a gamble.

Both major clouds sell the same idea under different names: Spot Instances on AWS, Spot VMs on Azure. You're buying spare GPU capacity the provider isn't currently using for on-demand or reserved customers, at a meaningfully lower price. In exchange, the provider can reclaim it on short notice - AWS gives a commonly cited interruption notice around two minutes; Azure evicts when it needs the capacity back, or when the spot price exceeds the max price you set. Neither cloud promises you when that happens - it could be five minutes in, or five days.

That short notice matters enormously more for training than for a stateless batch job. Interrupt a spot CPU instance running a batch job, and you lose a few minutes of cheap, easily redone work. Interrupt a spot GPU instance five hours into a training run with no checkpoint saved, and you lose every one of those GPU-hours at the GPU's already high rate, then start again from nothing. Same interruption, very different cost.

This is exactly why Chapter 3's checkpointing lesson matters here. A training job that saves model and optimizer state to durable storage every N steps or every few minutes only loses the work since its last checkpoint when it's interrupted - not the entire run. Pair that with a job orchestrator that catches the eviction notice, triggers an immediate save, and automatically relaunches on new spot capacity from that checkpoint, and the interruption becomes a short operational blip instead of a catastrophic loss.

So the decision to use spot GPUs for training and the decision about how aggressively to checkpoint aren't separate - tighter checkpointing is the price of taking the discount. Spot fits checkpoint-friendly training and disposable sweep runs well; it fits real-time inference serving poorly, since a dropped request isn't something a model endpoint can just resume from. Next lesson turns to a related sizing question: choosing the right GPU for training versus for inference.
